title: 柴油不是汽油：正渗入核心通胀，美联储还能说暂时吗？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: The rise in diesel prices does not stay in the energy line of CPI, which is exactly the kind of pass through the Fed cannot dismiss as transitory.
segments.zh: 柴油价格上涨不会只停留在CPI的能源项，这正是美联储无法将其视为暂时性因素的那种传导。

segments.en: Toast and joins us now for more. Toast and good morning. Morning. Great note.
segments.zh: Toast现在加入我们了解更多。Toast，早上好。早上好。很棒的笔记。

segments.en: Earlier this week, we all enjoyed reading it over several times.
segments.zh: 本周早些时候，我们都反复阅读了它。

segments.en: Are today's diesel prices tomorrow's core inflation?
segments.zh: 今天的柴油价格是明天的核心通胀吗？

segments.en: Is that how you see it? That is exactly the whole issue, because we normally differentiate inflation into two different pockets.
segments.zh: 你是这么看的吗？这正是整个问题的关键，因为我们通常将通胀分为两个不同的部分。

segments.en: One pocket is, of course, food and energy. And, of course, for a long, long time, we have all been saying, ah, we shouldn't look at food and energy.
segments.zh: 一个部分当然是食品和能源。而且，很长很长时间以来，我们一直说，啊，我们不应该看食品和能源。

segments.en: But what's really important about diesel is that food and energy normally means gas prices, meaning putting gas on your car.
segments.zh: 但柴油真正重要的是，食品和能源通常意味着汽油价格，也就是给车加油。

segments.en: But diesel is really, really important for transportation costs.
segments.zh: 但柴油对运输成本真的非常重要。

segments.en: So when diesel prices go up, when the crack spread widens out, that has had a really high correlation with rates, especially the long rates, because the market is concluding exactly that diesel prices
segments.zh: 所以当柴油价格上涨，当裂解价差扩大时，这与利率，尤其是长期利率有很高的相关性，因为市场正在得出这样的结论：柴油价格

segments.en: is not gas prices, because diesel prices go into transportation.
segments.zh: 不是汽油价格，因为柴油价格会进入运输成本。

segments.en: It goes into even services. So that means that, overall, when diesel prices go up, that is really entering elsewhere in the CPI basket,
segments.zh: 它甚至影响服务业。所以总体而言，当柴油价格上涨时，它实际上会渗透到CPI篮子的其他领域，而不仅仅是能源项。

segments.en: than in the energy line. How inelastic is diesel demand?
segments.zh: 柴油需求有多缺乏弹性？

segments.en: Well, that's also very inelastic, because, of course, transportation goods needs to come out to stores.
segments.zh: 嗯，这也非常缺乏弹性，因为运输货物需要运到商店。

segments.en: We need to have transportation of goods to build data centers. We need to cross the board so much of the economy relies on diesel prices.
segments.zh: 我们需要运输货物来建设数据中心。我们需要全面考虑，经济中如此多的领域都依赖柴油价格。

segments.en: So that's why when diesel prices go up, it's a good guess that a lot of this would be passed on to ultimately both firms, but also, of course, eventually consumers.
segments.zh: 所以这就是为什么当柴油价格上涨时，可以合理推测其中很大一部分最终会转嫁给企业，当然最终也会转嫁给消费者。

segments.en: So for that reason, the goal and the homework now for us in markets is to begin to quantify is no longer just about the energy line in the CPI baskets.
segments.zh: 因此，现在我们在市场中的目标和功课是开始量化，这不再仅仅是CPI篮子中的能源项。
